title: 1st Abyss 1st Matter In Negation There Is No Mutual Support

questions.question: In this passage, how does affirmation relate to other affirmations?
questions.answer: Each true affirmation backs up the others because they point to one shared reality.

questions.question: How is negation described differently from affirmation?
questions.answer: Negation is divided into many separate claims, since each person denies based on his own limited view.

questions.question: Why do many denials not become strong just because there are many of them?
questions.answer: Because those denials do not unite around one solid proof; they stay separate and cannot truly reinforce one another.

questions.question: What warning is given about the effect of denials on believers in this age?
questions.answer: They can plant doubts in weak people and damage the firmness of their faith.

questions.question: Who is especially said to have caused such doubts?
questions.answer: Certain European philosophers who spread denial and unbelief.

questions.question: What has happened to some people because of those doubts?
questions.answer: They lost certainty in faith and harmed their hope for everlasting happiness.

questions.question: How is death presented by deniers in a harmful way?
questions.answer: They portray it not as a passing from this world, but as total extinction.

questions.question: What effect does this view have on a person’s daily life?
questions.answer: It fills life with sorrow and fear because the grave seems like a doorway to nothingness.

questions.question: What does the passage say the grave constantly does for the denier?
questions.answer: It threatens him with destruction and makes life bitter.

questions.question: Based on the final sentence, how should faith be understood?
questions.answer: As a tremendous blessing and as something essential to real life.

questions.question: What is the main contrast made at the start of the passage?
questions.answer: It contrasts the unity of affirmation with the scattered nature of denial.

questions.question: Why is affirmation called “one”?
questions.answer: Because it reaches one common truth, so different affirmations support the same conclusion.

questions.question: Why does negation become “many”?
questions.answer: Because each denial comes from a person’s own opinion or personal belief rather than from a shared proof.

questions.question: What conclusion is drawn about the large number of unbelievers?
questions.answer: Their numbers do not give their position real weight against belief.

questions.question: What should be protected from doubt according to the passage?
questions.answer: A believer’s certainty and faith should be guarded.

questions.question: What has happened in this age that makes this protection especially necessary?
questions.answer: Ideas of denial have influenced some people and caused them to question faith.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the people who were misled by these ideas?
questions.answer: It describes them as unfortunate and easily deceived.

questions.question: How does unbelief change the meaning of death?
questions.answer: It strips death of any hopeful meaning and treats it as complete nonexistence.

questions.question: What emotional result comes from seeing the grave this way?
questions.answer: It produces deep sadness and a constant sense of dread.

questions.question: What final lesson is the reader asked to recognize?
questions.answer: The reader is asked to realize how precious faith is and how central it is to a meaningful life.

questions.question: According to the passage, what happens when people make positive claims about truth?
questions.answer: Their claims can strengthen one another because they are connected to the same truth.

questions.question: What prevents negative claims from giving each other the same support?
questions.answer: They come from separate personal judgments and do not rest on one united foundation.

questions.question: Does the passage treat the popularity of unbelief as proof of its truth? Explain.
questions.answer: No. It says large numbers and outward dominance do not give unbelief real value against belief.

questions.question: What responsibility is mentioned toward the faith of a believer?
questions.answer: People should avoid causing uncertainty in a believer’s heart.

questions.question: What source of doubt is named in the passage?
questions.answer: Denials coming from European philosophical thought.

questions.question: What damage did those denials cause in some people?
questions.answer: They ruined their confidence in faith and led them away from eternal success.

questions.question: In the denier’s outlook, what does death become?
questions.answer: It becomes a final end with no continuing life beyond it.

questions.question: Why does the grave become so frightening in that outlook?
questions.answer: Because it appears to open only to annihilation, not to any future hope.

questions.question: What does this outlook do to the sweetness of life?
questions.answer: It poisons life with intense grief and bitterness.

questions.question: What is implied about faith by calling it the essence of life?
questions.answer: It means faith gives life its deepest meaning, value, and hope.

questions.question: What principle about affirmation is stated in the passage?
questions.answer: Positive testimony to truth leads to one result, so the different testimonies support each other.

questions.question: What principle about negation is stated in the passage?
questions.answer: Negative claims split into many separate results because they depend on individual viewpoints.

questions.question: Why can’t unbelievers rely on their greater numbers as a strong argument?
questions.answer: Because a crowd of separate denials does not become solid proof merely by being large.

questions.question: What does the passage say should not be disturbed in a believer?
questions.answer: The firmness of faith and certainty should not be shaken.

questions.question: What kind of intellectual influence is blamed for spreading doubts?
questions.answer: Philosophical denials coming from Europe.

questions.question: How are the people affected by these doubts portrayed morally and emotionally?
questions.answer: They are shown as pitiable people who were misled and harmed.

questions.question: What meaning of death is lost when faith is denied?
questions.answer: Its meaning as a departure from this world is lost.

questions.question: What false meaning is then given to death?
questions.answer: It is treated as everlasting destruction.

questions.question: How does the passage connect the grave with the denier’s mental state?
questions.answer: The grave becomes a constant source of fear that overshadows his life.

questions.question: What two things is faith described as at the end?
questions.answer: A great gift and the core of life itself.

questions.question: If several people affirm a truth, what relationship do their statements have to one another in this passage?
questions.answer: They reinforce one another because they agree on the same reality.

questions.question: If several people deny a truth, what relationship do their statements have to one another?
questions.answer: They remain separate and weak because each one rests on a private perspective.

questions.question: What mistaken assumption about unbelief is the passage trying to remove?
questions.answer: The assumption that unbelief becomes strong simply because many people hold it.

questions.question: What harmful action regarding a believer’s heart is the passage warning against?
questions.answer: Introducing doubts that weaken settled faith.

questions.question: Which group’s ideas are said to have spread such doubt in modern times?
questions.answer: Certain philosophers from Europe.

questions.question: What was the spiritual cost for some who followed those ideas?
questions.answer: They lost certainty and damaged their chance of eternal joy.

questions.question: What does unbelief make people think death means?
questions.answer: It makes them think death is total disappearance.

questions.question: What does that belief do to a person’s experience of the grave?
questions.answer: It makes the grave seem like an always-open entrance to annihilation.

questions.question: What attitude does the passage encourage toward faith?
questions.answer: Gratitude and deep appreciation for it as life’s greatest blessing.

questions.question: Summarize the difference between affirmation and negation in one sentence based on the passage.
questions.answer: Affirmation gathers strength through shared truth, while negation stays divided through personal denial.

questions.question: Why does personal viewpoint make negation weaker?
questions.answer: Because each denial is tied to one individual’s limited outlook instead of a common established reality.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the apparent dominance of deniers?
questions.answer: It says that outward majority does not give them true importance against belief.

questions.question: What should a careful person avoid doing to believers?
questions.answer: Causing uncertainty in their conviction.

questions.question: In this passage, what role did some European philosophers play?
questions.answer: They became a source of skeptical ideas that unsettled some people’s faith.

questions.question: What kind of people were especially harmed by these ideas?
questions.answer: Those who were vulnerable, easily deceived, and spiritually unfortunate.

questions.question: How does the passage compare the believer’s and denier’s understanding of death?
questions.answer: The believer can see death with meaning, while the denier sees it as final extinction.

questions.question: What image is used to show the constant pressure unbelief places on a person?
questions.answer: The image of the grave standing open and continually threatening destruction.

questions.question: What emotional condition follows from that unbelieving view?
questions.answer: Ongoing misery, fear, and bitterness.

questions.question: What is the final message of the passage about faith?
questions.answer: Faith is not a small extra in life; it is a huge blessing and the very foundation of true life.
